title: 1998 AHSME Problem 18
statement: A right circular cone of volume \(A,\) a right circular cylinder of volume \(M,\) and a sphere of volume \(C\) all have the same radius, and the common height of the cone and the cylinder is equal to the diameter of the sphere. Then

solutions.text: The volumes are \(A=\frac23\pi r^3,\) \(M=2\pi r^3,\) and \(C=\frac43\pi r^3.\) Therefore \(A-M+C\) \(=(\frac{2}{3}-2+\frac{4}{3})\pi r^3=0,\) so A is correct.
hints: Let the common radius be \(r\), so the cone and cylinder height is \(2r\)
Write all three volumes as multiples of \(\pi r^3\)
